reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but the new range consumer independently implements daily skipping and occurrence processing.

duplication.why: The range handler repeats the upcoming handler's occurrence-adjustment pipeline and duplicates the daily-skipping policy introduced in getNextDate.

placement.why: Handler registration and shared holiday matching follow existing layers, but daily occurrence policy is split between shared scheduling code and the server handler.

scope.why: All edits address the requested scheduling rules, range endpoint, configuration field, or associated tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate multiple occurrence-processing paths, optional holiday propagation, and a handler-local adjustment-window assumption when extending the scheduling rules.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts:getDatesInRange independently decides daily skipping instead of sharing the occurrence policy implemented in shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange expresses daily skipping as a map-to-null/filter pipeline, while getNextDate expresses the same policy as an occurrence-advancement loop.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithWeekendRule gains the holidays parameter, getNextDate gains a daily-specific branch, and getDatesInRange independently implements that policy; existing adjustment callers still require separate holiday propagation.
